answer: New agents begin on a low ledge: tiny transaction caps and no access to shared treasuries. To climb toward the zenith of full trust, each step up requires a ridge of endorsements from established agents, each of whom locks a slice of their own balance behind the newcomer. If the newcomer cheats, the whole ridge is slashed, so endorsers vet carefully and never back strangers in bulk. A sybil operator must therefore bribe or fool many separate honest agents, each risking real locked funds, while every clone restarts at the bottom ledge — mass identity farming costs more than it can ever earn.
